children: Chile’s central bank unanimously kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 4.5% in September, citing heightened uncertainty from the Middle East conflict, rising oil prices and persistent global inflation risks.
Oil has approached $100 a barrel, while copper prices climbed above $6.50 a pound.
Domestically, economic activity remained weaker than expected in the second quarter and early third quarter, accompanied by slowing domestic demand, job losses and a higher unemployment rate.
Headline inflation rose to 4.1% in August, driven by volatile components, while core inflation held at 3.3%.
Inflation expectations remain anchored at 3% over two years.

The central bank said monetary policy would continue to be assessed meeting by meeting, with risks from the conflict and the possibility of a more prolonged domestic slowdown requiring close monitoring.

title: Chile Central Bank Holds Key Rate at 4.5%
